entries.answer: First I stay calm and sit with her. I gently ask why she does not want the medicine, maybe it tastes bad or she feels sick. I would never force it. I check the chart to confirm the right tablet and time, then offer it again after 15 minutes with some water or food. If she still refuses I write it in the care notes and call the nurse and her son to inform them.
I will lift her up quickly and put her on the bed so she is comfortable, then give her a painkiller and tell her family in the evening.

I would not go home till the next person comes. I'd ring the agency office and the relief carer to find out where she is, and while waiting I keep an eye on uncle. When she reaches I explain everything that happened in the night and write it in the register.
Calm, patience, dignity, respect, medicine schedule, family communication, care plan.
Madam fell means first i will not move her, i will call 108 ambulance and tell to her son also. I will sit near her till ambulance comes.
I will wait.
I won't shout at her or force the tablet. I'll talk to her softly and try again after dinner. If she still says no I let the nurse know.
I will handle the situation properly and do whatever is needed for her.

Step one, I keep my voice low and calm and don't argue with her. I ask her what is bothering her — sometimes the tablet is big or she has a stomach ache. I check the medicine box and the chart to make sure it is the right dose for the evening. I explain kindly what the medicine is for and offer it with a little juice. If she still refuses after a second try I don't force it; I note it in the log and inform the nurse and her daughter on the phone, and check with her again before bed.
I will explain to her that the medicine is important for her health and try to convince her nicely. If she does not take it I will tell her family.
She has to take it, so I will hold her hand firmly and put the tablet in her mouth with water. Old people become stubborn, you have to be strict.
I will give the medicine.

Sit beside her and hold her hand, ask her softly what's wrong. Maybe the pill is hard to swallow — I'd crush it only if the nurse says it's okay, or give it with a banana. Mark it in the chart either way, and ring her son so he knows.

First i will tell her very politely aunty ji please take medicine it is for your BP. If she not taking i will wait 10 min and again try. Still not taking then i will inform to madam and write in book.
I have worked 5 years as a caregiver in Pune and I am very hardworking and honest person.

I would not try to lift her because the hip may be broken. First I check she is breathing and talking properly and ask where it hurts. I call 108 for an ambulance and then call my supervisor. I put a pillow under her head and a blanket on her to keep her warm, and tell her help is coming so she doesn't panic. Then I inform her family and when the ambulance arrives I tell them how I found her and what time.
I will help her stand up slowly and walk her to the bed, then put some balm on the hip and let her rest.
I will call the ambulance and her family immediately and stay with her.

Keep her exactly where she is on the floor, don't try to get her up. Ask her if she hit her head and see if she's breathing okay. Dial 112, then the office. Cover her with a shawl and hold her hand, talk to her so she stays calm till the ambulance people come.
I will take care of her and manage the situation as required.
Emergency, ambulance, first aid, hospital, 108, calm, safety, dignity.

Uncle fell down na, so first i check he is talking or not. I will not lift him alone because bone may be broken. Call to 108 and his son. Till ambulance come i will give him water and keep him comfortable on floor with pillow.
I will call someone to help me pick her up.

I can't leave the client alone, so I stay until my replacement arrives. I call her to check where she is and how long she will take, and I inform my supervisor at the agency about the delay. I also message the family so they know. When she comes I give a full handover — medicines given, food, any problems — and write the delay and handover time in the logbook.
My shift is over so I will leave at the time. The client is sleeping anyway, the replacement will come soon.
I will call the replacement and ask when she is coming and wait for her.

Stick around till the night person shows up — never walk out on a patient. Ring her up, and if she isn't picking up, ring the agency. Once she's there, fill her in on everything and jot the times down.
I will wait only, no problem. I will call to office and tell sir that relief has not come. When she come i will tell her all the things about uncle.
Wait and call her.
Calm is important. Dignity is important. Respect is important. Medicine schedule is important. Family is important.
I will manage the situation properly and do my duty.
